title: Share the roadmap and set expectations
summary: A roadmap only helps if people understand it. Share it in a way each audience can use, be clear about what is certain and what is not, and keep it up to date.

beginner: Decide who needs the roadmap: your team, leaders, other teams, customers or the public. Each needs a different level of detail.
Show outcomes and problems, not just features. For each item, say why it matters.
Use a simple format such as Now, Next and Later, so certainty drops as items move further away.
Say clearly what is not on the roadmap and why.
Walk key stakeholders through it in person and invite questions.
Agree when you will update it and where people can always find the latest version.
intermediate: Tailor roadmap views for each audience.
Frame items as outcomes, with confidence shown by time horizon.
Present it, take questions and record concerns.
Publish one source of truth and an update rhythm.
experienced: Use the roadmap to tell the strategy story: where you are going, why and what you are trading off.
Pre-wire senior stakeholders so the review is a confirmation, not a surprise.
Treat changes as normal and explain them openly when they happen.
Align roadmaps across teams so dependencies are visible.

canDelegateTo.task: Keep the roadmap and delivery plan in step
Make the roadmap wording clear for each audience

toolExamples.jira: Publish a read-only roadmap view for leaders so they see live status without extra reports.
toolExamples.confluence: Embed the roadmap on one page with a short explanation of each outcome.
toolExamples.miro: Draw a Now, Next, Later board for workshops with stakeholders.
toolExamples.notion: Keep a roadmap database with a view per audience.

definitionOfDone: Roadmap views agreed for each audience
Items framed as outcomes with confidence shown
Shared and walked through with key stakeholders
Single source of truth and update rhythm agreed
pitfalls: Treating the roadmap as a promise of dates
Letting it go out of date so people stop trusting it

leaderView.good: Each audience gets a roadmap they can use, with clear confidence levels.
ask: Who has seen the roadmap, and what did they push back on?
How do we show what's firm and what's uncertain?
